description: The orhr_col-style Householder RECONSTRUCTION (panel_solve_fused + diag_lu_warp) is co-dominant in two paths: ~31% of the n4096 CholeskyQR (brief-2) and ~6ms of the n512 CQR2 (brief-15) -- it is a per-panel serial LU of (Q - diag), a 2nd serial factorization. Attack it directly: multi-CTA-per-matrix and/or tensor-core the recon's panel-LU so it stops being a serial single-CTA chain. A faster recon makes BOTH the large-n CholeskyQR and the n512 int-Ozaki CQR2 viable. Profile the recon kernels first to find the dominant one, then split/tensor-core it. Stock-only (no BF16x9; OB64/IB32).

Activate CholeskyQR+orhr_col recon at n4096 B2 (_HH_QR=0 vs parent's _HH_QR=1 Householder). shape6 54522->13158us (4.1x), geomean 1879.37->1660.58. Profile (n4096): recon = panel_solve_fused 16.2% + diag_lu_warp 10.4% + build_H 0.8% ~= 27% of the path; FP64 getrf_wo_pivot Gram-chol = 26.4%; trsm_right (Q=AR^-1) 6.3%; int8-Ozaki Gram 5.2%. panel_solve_fused DOMINATES the recon. validate PASS (orth 0.382/gate, factor 0.00854). Margin: factor 0.00854 (gate 1.0 scaled), orth 0.382.

_CHOL_FP32=0 (plain FP64 Dpotrf) recovers the fastest cholesky base: shape6 13158->11204us, geomean 1660.58->1650.73. The mode-2 tensor-core blocked cholesky added trailing GEMMs atop FP64 diag blocks so it was slower. This is the clean base for attacking the recon (panel_solve_fused+diag_lu_warp, ~31% of the now-11.2ms path). validate PASS, n4096 B2 scored: factor 0.0135, orth 0.42 (gate 1.0 scaled). Comfortable margins.
